- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting it underestimates downward trends or fails to adjust for seasonality.
- Model often lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward corrections — should adjust for delayed reaction to market signals.
- Forecasts show strong persistence of recent high values (e.g., 70–80) but fail to decay toward lower mean — should incorporate exponential smoothing or moving average decay for mean reversion.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, especially when true values show sudden drops — should add volatility weighting or adaptive variance adjustment.
